speaker: Mr Dennis Tan Lip Fong
text: asked the Minister for Home Affairs (a) what is the cause of the oil leak at the Brani Regional Base of the Police Coast Guard on 5 February 2025 which has resulted in 23 tonnes of diesel being leaked into the waters south of Singapore; (b) whether there will be a formal investigation to ascertain the causes of the oil leak; and (c) if so, whether the full findings can be made known to the public.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The contractor was unaware about the report of oil leakage at this point and had acted independently.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: After carrying out its checks, PCG confirmed that the leak was from this damaged hose and verified that there were no signs of other leaks around Brani Base.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: PCG updated MPA of the situation at around 5.50 pm.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Agencies commenced measures to mitigate the impact, including Sentosa Development Corporation which laid booms to prevent any oil from reaching the beaches.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On the morning of 6 February 2025, MPA and PCG flew drones over the waters in the vicinity of Brani Base and the Southern Islands to get a clearer assessment of the impact and also activated an oil cleaning contractor to assist with the clean-up operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: During this period, navigational traffic was not affected, the operations in the Port of Singapore were able to continue unimpacted, and no beaches were closed.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: On 8 February 2025, MPA and PCG stood down the clean-up operations.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: PCG was unaware of any leaks at that point.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: That morning, an auxiliary police officer (APO) deployed in PCG had reported at 11.57 am that water was leaking from the affected hose at the pontoon.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As there were both fuel and water hoses at the pontoon, and the APO was not trained to identify oil leaks, he had mistakenly reported it to be a water leak.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Marine diesel appears as a clear transparent fluid, so he thought it was water.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Pursuant to the APO’s report, a PCG officer arrived at about 12.25 pm to do further checks but did not observe any leak.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: There was no visible oil sheen on the water in the area and no noticeable smell of leaked fuel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The facilities management staff arrived subsequently at 1.38 pm to conduct further checks as part of PCG’s fault reporting protocol for leaks.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: The staff did not observe any oil sheen on the water, and there was no noticeable smell of fuel.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: As both the PCG officer and facilities management staff had observed no sign of discharge of oil into the water, it was assessed that the leak reported by the APO was indeed a water leak.

speaker: The Minister of State for Home Affairs (Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: A case was lodged for the rectification of a water leak.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: Minister of State, you might want to wrap up.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The leak was finally stopped at about 3.40 pm when the contractor spotted the leak and isolated the main valve, as I explained earlier.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: The fuel hoses are checked and maintained every month.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Following the oil leak at Brani Base, PCG promptly inspected all fuel hoses there on 6 February 2025.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: Similar checks were completed on 8 February 2025 at its three other bases – Loyang, Lim Chu Kang and Gul Regional Bases.

speaker: Assoc Prof Dr Muhammad Faishal Ibrahim
text: While PCG’s maintenance and reporting protocols are generally consistent with industry best practices, PCG is reviewing them nevertheless to further reduce the likelihood of leaks of such magnitude in the future.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: The Clerk will now proceed to read the Order of the day.

speaker: Mr Speaker
text: [Pursuant to Standing Order No 22(3), provided that Members had not asked for questions standing in their names to be postponed to a later Sitting day or withdrawn, written answers to questions not reached by the end of Question Time are reproduced in the Appendix.]
